PICK.text: Bolted to the wall with industrial bolts. Adrian learned from the doormat.

OPEN.text: I poke around the menus. 'ADMIN ACCESS REQUIRED. Nice try, Patient Zero.' It knows my nickname.

CLOSE.text: I look for the off switch. There isn't one. This screen was built not to let me leave.

PUSH.text: I push the monitor. It doesn't budge. It's the most stable thing I've met all year.

PULL.text: I peek behind the monitor. Wires, dust, and one very old moth. It followed me here too.

GIVE.text: The monitor already has my whole file. Giving it more feels like oversharing.

LOOK.text: Charts nailed to every inch of wall. 'THIS IS THE BOTTOM', seven times, at seven prices. The handwriting is mine.

USE.text: I trace the timeline with a finger. It starts with 'FIRST MINT!' and a smiley. It ends with 'Again.'

TALK.text: I read them aloud. 'Buy here.' 'Sell here.' 'Why didn't I sell here.' It's my own diary. Out loud. Ugh.

PICK.text: I pull one chart off the wall. There's another chart behind it. Then another. I stop before I find wallpaper.

OPEN.text: A rolled-up chart in the corner, covered in red Xs. Same leaky blue ink as Adrian's pen. Somebody marked my mistakes for me.

CLOSE.text: I pin the chart back up. Crooked. Whoever made these would hate that. ...I hate that.

PUSH.text: I push a stack of charts aside. They slide to the floor. I don't pick them up. Growth.

PULL.text: A sticky note falls off a chart: 'This is not financial advice. This is a cry for help.' My handwriting again.

GIVE.text: The walls have enough charts. One more and the building falls over.

keycard: No reader on the exit. Getting out is free. Getting in was the expensive part.

CLOSE.text: You can't close a floor. I checked. I'm thorough now. It's a whole thing.

PUSH.text: I stamp on the floor. Solid. Somewhere below, Chad probably calls it a vibe.

PULL.text: I try to lift a floor tile. It's glued down. Adrian glues everything down. Doormats. Tiles. Me.

GIVE.text: The floor already has my footprints. Old ones too, apparently.

LOOK.text: A plaque: 'To the Founders who believed before anyone else.' Below it, my wallet address. I don't remember donating.

USE.text: I run a finger over my engraved address. Warm brass. Patient Zero, founder. Somebody polishes this weekly.

TALK.text: 'Was it worth it?' I ask the plaque. My reflection in the brass shrugs.

LOOK.text: Pipes and cables tangled across the ceiling, patched with duct tape. The whole clinic is one sneeze from a flood.

USE.text: I reach for a dangling cable. Then I remember I like my eyebrows. I leave it dangling.

TALK.text: 'Who wired you?' The cables hang there. Whoever it was, they gave up halfway. Relatable.

PICK.text: I tug a loose cable. The lights flicker. I let go and pretend that was somebody else.

OPEN.text: I pry open a junction box. Inside: wires labeled 'DATA IN', 'DATA OUT', and one labeled 'PATIENT ZERO MONITORING'. Ominous.

CLOSE.text: I snap the junction box shut. Whatever 'PATIENT ZERO MONITORING' does, it can do it without my fingers.

PUSH.text: I push a pipe. It groans. The ceiling shudders. I stop pushing things in this building.

PULL.text: I pull a cable. Somewhere upstairs, something beeps. I let go. Nurse Gwei will blame the ghosts.

GIVE.text: The pipes need a plumber. I'm a detective. We'd just stare at each other.

USE.text: I sip the water. Stale. Fernando would still drink it. Fernando drinks anything.

TALK.text: 'Table, tell me your secrets.' It holds its glass and says nothing. Strong, silent, metal.

PICK.text: I pull a shard from the frame. It shows my face in green monitor light. I put it back. I've seen enough of me.

OPEN.text: No door to the observation room from this side. They could watch. They weren't allowed to help.

CLOSE.text: You can't close a broken window. You can only stop leaning on it.

PUSH.text: I push the glass. A chunk crashes into the other room. Very loud. Somewhere, Nurse Gwei starts a form.

PULL.text: I tug the frame. It holds. The frame is fine. Only the glass had a breakdown.

GIVE.text: The window has already been given enough. Someone's fist, by the look of it. Possibly mine.

LOOK.text: Thick cables run from the chair into holes in the floor. Some carry data. Some carry... I'd rather not know.

USE.text: I follow a cable with my hand. Warm. Pulsing. Whatever this chair feeds, it never shut down. It's been waiting.

TALK.text: 'Where do you go?' The cables hum. They know. They just don't talk to patients.

PICK.text: I tug a cable. It's bolted down. Everything in this room is bolted down except my sanity.

OPEN.text: Under a floor panel: a box labeled 'BIOMETRIC FEED — TREATMENT SUITE A.' The chair reads more than wallets.

CLOSE.text: I push the floor panel back. 'BIOMETRIC FEED' disappears. My pulse doesn't.

PUSH.text: I step on the cables. They don't even notice. Built to outlast the patients. Rude, but accurate.

PULL.text: I yank a thin cable. Sparks. The monitor flickers. I plug it back in and whistle innocently.

GIVE.text: The cables already carry enough. Mostly me, apparently.

LOOK.text: Peeling paint, water damage, dark stains that could be rust or... I'm going to say rust.

USE.text: I scrape the paint. A dozen layers, each a slightly different white. Somebody had a lot of meetings about this.

TALK.text: 'How many treatments have you seen?' The wall drops a paint flake on my shoe. Passive-aggressive. DOORIS would like it.

PICK.text: I peel off a strip of paint. Behind it, someone scratched into the plaster: 'NGMI.' Below that, in different handwriting: 'WAGMI.' Below that: 'We didn't.'

OPEN.text: Behind a crack in the plaster, an old blueprint: 'RECONDITIONING BAY 01.' Not treatment. Reconditioning. Lovely.

CLOSE.text: I press the paint flap back. It curls away again. Some things refuse to stay covered up.

PUSH.text: I push the wall. Solid under the rot. Good bones, bad skin. Like me, the doctor would say.

PULL.text: I pull a chunk of plaster free. Dust everywhere. Behind it, bare concrete. And a moth, looking annoyed.

GIVE.text: The wall has had enough. Time, damp, and whoever punched that dent. I'm not adding to the list.
